description: VisWaterNet contains Python tools for visualising water-distribution networks and their simulation results. Its contributors publish routines that place continuous or discretised values on network nodes and links, customise reservoirs, tanks, valves and pumps, and animate results across time steps. The README lists WNTR, NetworkX, Matplotlib, Pandas and NumPy among its dependencies. Geographic coverage and the displayed period follow the supplied network and result series; the software does not prescribe spatial or temporal resolution. It can import Excel data or values generated in Python and produce network figures and GIF animations. Code is available on GitHub and through PyPI under the MIT licence, with no software charge. A limitation is that this is an analysis and plotting toolkit, not an independent hydraulic model. It can help inspect pressure, flow and resilience-study outputs and communicate differences between scenarios. Related record model-wntr supplies a documented dependency, and model-epanet represents a related distribution-network simulator. Only package documentation and metadata were checked; no network model or plotting example was executed. The code is available free of charge under its stated licence.
name: VisWaterNet
notes: G5 G5-0013. Software portability is recorded as global, not worldwide validation. Metadata and documentation checked; software not executed. Independent validation and maintenance commitment not established. The modelling_suite vocabulary is used for this simulation-analysis toolkit. It visualises network simulation outputs; it does not implement a separate hydraulic solver.
